messages:
incident-bot: :warning: Observability alert — Datadog ingestion latency detected for prod metrics/logs/APM. >90th percentile write delay 6m. Triggered by `obs.ingest.latency.prod` > 5m for 3m. https://status.datadoghq.com/incident/abc-123
matt_sre: Paging @here — I'm on call. Starting investigation. Can people avoid large deploys while we triage?
emily_prodeng: seeing the same on dashboards. Traces are patchy in the service map. Customers reporting slow error pages from frontend (not sure if related).
matt_sre: first quick checks: Datadog API auth ok, but ingestion backlog shows ~120k events queued in the forwarder. Prom metrics (our internal) for forwarding success rate dropping to 60%.
raj_frontend: any idea if it's logs only or metrics too? Our synthetic checks still show app metrics in prometheus.
matt_sre: looks like logs + APM spans are delayed. System metrics (node/cpu) still streaming via prometheus -> grafana. So core infra monitoring intact. We likely have a vendor-side processing/backoff.
datadog-status-bot: Datadog status update: Customers may experience delayed ingestion and partial UI inconsistencies. Link: https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/abc-123
emily_prodeng: tagging @dan_cs — please start a short customer impact triage: which paid customers on Dedicated or Private might notice missing traces/logs?
dan_cs: will pull roster and ping top 5 accounts (enterprise) with proactive note. ETA 15m.
matt_sre: Mitigation plan (short):
1) confirm whether our forwarder is retrying or dropping — `kubectl -n observability logs dd-forwarder-0 --tail 200`
2) open Datadog support ticket (done, internal ref: RW-OBS-2024-57)
3) enable backup log sink to S3 for critical services (already configured but not active) — I will enable for prod-apps
4) relax automated alerting to avoid pager spam once we have clear degradation window

Example command I'm running:
```
kubectl -n observability exec -it dd-forwarder-0 -- sh -c "grep -i backlog /var/log/datadog/forwarder.log | tail -n 50"
```
matt_sre: logs show `503 response from intake` and `rate limited by remote` errors. So vendor-side throttling.
raj_frontend: any temporary app-side knobs we should flip? reduce tracing sampling?
emily_prodeng: yes — reduce trace sampling to 0.1 for non-critical services, keep 1.0 for payment/auth flows. Raj can you deploy sampling override?
raj_frontend: deploying sampling override now to prod (small rollout). Will share deployment id.
raj_frontend: rollout  -> `deploy/sampling-overrides  rev: a3f2` (started) :white_check_mark:
matt_sre: enabling S3 fallback for logs for `payments`, `auth`, `api-gateway`. Command:
```
# enable backup sink flag in forwarder config
kubectl -n observability patch cm dd-forwarder-config -p '{"data":{"backup_s3":"true"}}'
kubectl -n observability rollout restart deploy/dd-forwarder
```
matt_sre: opened support ticket with Datadog, CC'ed Enterprise support. Ticket#: DD-987654. They acknowledge degraded processing in `US` intake region and are investigating.
dan_cs: initial outreach: emailed top 3 enterprise customers, said we are investigating an observability ingestion slowdown (third-party). Offered scheduled call if they want immediate updates. Waiting replies.
emily_prodeng: Logging the incident in our tracker RW-INC-2024-184. Short summary: Datadog ingestion delays causing partial observability blindspots for logs/APM; infra metrics still ok.
incident-bot: Incident created RW-INC-2024-184, severity: S3 (impacting debugging/observability), assignee: matt_sre. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/RW-INC-2024-184
matt_sre: Practical checks to reduce pain for oncall:
- disable low-value alerts (errors 400-499 spikes) for 1h
- set dashboard refresh to 30s (avoid automatic heavy poll)
- prefer internal prometheus for paging-critical alerts
I'll toggle those now.

matt_sre: Done: quieted ~12 alerts (errors, verbose logs). Switched critical alerts to prometheus rules.
zara_platform: I'm taking next shift starting in 45m. Please add runbook notes and handoff checklist.
matt_sre: Handoff note (for @zara_platform):
- Datadog is experiencing region ingestion delays (ticket DD-987654)
- Backup S3 sink enabled for payments/auth/api-gateway
- Trace sampling lowered globally to 10% except critical flows
- Prometheus-based alerts are active for uptime/latency
- Datadog UI gaps expected until vendor resolves; check DD ticket for updates
- Customer outreach in progress by @dan_cs
- Incident tracker RW-INC-2024-184 has timeline + commands used

zara_platform: ack — I'll monitor and escalate if Datadog confirms processing backlog cleared. If vendor doesn't resolve in 3h, we escalate to oncall lead for possible cross-region failover or ingestion re-route.
emily_prodeng: note for postmortem: confirm whether our forwarder should have circuit-breaker that flips to backup automatically instead of manual toggle.
dan_cs: got a reply from one customer — they saw missing traces for ~20m, appreciated proactive note. They're asking for final RCA once resolved.
matt_sre: Datadog updated ticket: "Mitigation in progress, backlog decreasing". They estimate 60–90m to clear fully. Monitoring backlog metrics.

matt_sre: backlog trend (internal): `obs.forwarder.backlog.count` -> 120k -> 40k over 25m. Good sign.

datadog-status-bot: Update: Datadog intake region is recovering; delayed ingestion is improving but some customers still affected. https://status.datadoghq.com
matt_sre: marking this thread for handoff in 30m. If anything changes escalate immediately. :triangular_flag_on_post:
zara_platform: Thanks — taking over in 30. I'll put a pinned note in the incident doc and set a reminder for 3h to reassess.

matt_sre: final: summary for handoff to @zara_platform and next oncall: vendor-side ingestion delay caused partial observability blindspots for logs/APM. We mitigated with sampling change + S3 fallback + quieting alerts. Customer outreach ongoing. Ticket DD-987654 linked. RW-INC-2024-184 updated.
